- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≥0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk premium or market panic.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if price is trending sharply upward, forecast should not continue rising beyond 2–3 days unless sentiment confirms sustained momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative in last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model is overconfident; apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overfitting to recent calm.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00 (e.g., strong bullish signal), model often fails to reflect true market sentiment; increase forecast by 5–10% to align with sentiment intensity.
